title: Average Order Value by Acquisition Channel
description: For each customer acquisition channel, calculate the **number of orders**, **average order value** (AOV), and **total revenue**. Order by AOV descending to see which channel drives the highest-value purchases.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE orders (order_id INT, customer_id INT, channel VARCHAR(50), amount DECIMAL(10,2)); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1,1,'Organic Search',150.00),(2,2,'Organic Search',200.00),(3,3,'Organic Search',175.00),(4,4,'Paid Ads',300.00),(5,5,'Paid Ads',250.00),(6,6,'Paid Ads',400.00),(7,7,'Paid Ads',350.00),(8,8,'Email',120.00),(9,9,'Email',180.00),(10,10,'Email',160.00),(11,11,'Social Media',80.00),(12,12,'Social Media',95.00);
solution_sql: SELECT channel, COUNT(*) AS order_count, ROUND(AVG(amount), 2) AS avg_order_value, SUM(amount) AS total_revenue FROM orders GROUP BY channel ORDER BY avg_order_value DESC

test_cases.description: 4 channels: Paid Ads AOV=325.00, Organic Search AOV=175.00, Email AOV=153.33, Social Media AOV=87.50

hints: GROUP BY channel and apply COUNT(*), AVG(amount), and SUM(amount) to get the three metrics in a single query.
ROUND(AVG(amount), 2) rounds the average to 2 decimal places — without rounding you may get many decimal digits.
explanation: Grouping by channel produces metrics per acquisition source. Paid Ads: 4 orders (300+250+400+350)/4=325.00 AOV, $1300 total. Organic Search: 3 orders, AOV=175.00, $525 total. Email: 3 orders, AOV=153.33, $460 total. Social Media: 2 orders, AOV=87.50, $175 total. Despite Social Media having the lowest AOV, Paid Ads drives the most revenue per customer — key insight for budget allocation.
